_meta.description: Buildable structures and vehicle parameters, owned by Member 2. Costs, build times, and output figures are editable gameplay-balance values, not NASA measurements; revisit them during the Day 16 balance pass. build_cost.power is the one-time construction energy demand.

structures.name: Solar Array
structures.effect: Gameplay effect: adds 18 kWh of potential generation per sol before the selected site's illumination modifier. Intended as the affordable early power investment.

structures.name: Water Extractor
structures.effect: Gameplay effect: after a rover prospect has been investigated, adds up to 16 L of water recovery per sol. Output must be separately tuned and must not be calculated directly from LEND hydrogen readings.

structures.name: Greenhouse Module
structures.effect: Gameplay effect: produces 1.2 kg dry food per sol while consuming 6 kWh and 4 L water per sol. Intended to offset, but not completely erase, the four-person food draw.

structures.name: Radiation Shielding Wall
structures.effect: Gameplay effect: reduces the crew's unshielded radiation dose by 25%. This stacks with terrain shielding only when the simulation integration defines the combination rule.

structures.name: Habitat Extension
structures.effect: Gameplay effect: adds two crew-capacity slots and reduces aggregate crew-stress gain by 15%. It is deliberately a late, expensive resilience upgrade.

structures.name: Comms Relay
structures.effect: Gameplay effect: unlocks one-sol advance warning for solar-particle events, allowing a shelter choice before the radiation effect is applied.

rover.notes: Power cost is derived from NASA VIPER planning data: 397 W typical direct-drive load / 0.72 km/h top speed = about 0.55 kWh/km (NASA NTRS 2020 VIPER Mission Overview; NASA Science VIPER In Depth, read 2026-09-27). The 6 km per-sol round-trip cap is a gameplay scheduling assumption, not a NASA rover specification; VIPER's separately reported 20 km range is not treated as a one-sol allowance. Discovery probability is also a gameplay balance value, not a NASA measurement: roll independently for each newly explored kilometre (about 35% cumulative chance at 6 km).
